# Week 1 — Free movement of goods

> **In one glance** Dassonville (Case 8/74, para 5): "all trading rules enacted by Member States which are capable of hindering, directly or indirectly, actually or potentially, intra-Community trade are to be considered as measures having an effect equivalent to quantitative restrictions". Keck (Joined Cases C-267/91 and C-268/91, para 16): "contrary to what has previously been decided" certain selling arrangements fall outside that formula.

## The Dassonville formula
*Dassonville* (Case 8/74, judgment of 11 July 1974) defined a measure having equivalent effect to a quantitative restriction (an MEQR) broadly. The prohibitions sit in Art 34 TFEU (imports) and Art 35 TFEU (exports), and the derogation grounds in Art 36 TFEU. The old numbering ran Articles 30 to 36 EEC, then 28 to 30 EC, now 34 to 36 TFEU.

## Mutual recognition and mandatory requirements
*Cassis de Dijon* (Case 120/78, judgment of 20 February 1979) is the source of mutual recognition. The Court found no valid reason why goods lawfully produced and marketed in one Member State should not be introduced into another, and it accepted mandatory requirements (fiscal supervision, public health, fairness of commercial transactions, consumer defence) as a ground beside Article 36 TFEU.

## Selling arrangements
*Keck and Mithouard* (Joined Cases C-267/91 and C-268/91, judgment of 24 November 1993) separates product requirements, which remain MEQRs, from certain selling arrangements. Such rules fall outside the Dassonville formula if they apply to all relevant traders and affect domestic and imported products in the same manner, in law and in fact.

## Market access
*Commission v Italy* (Case C-110/05, judgment of 10 February 2009) sums up the case law in three limbs, the third being any other measure which hinders access of products to the market, and applies it to a rule on the use of a product. *Ker-Optika* (Case C-108/09, judgment of 2 December 2010) applies Keck to an internet sales ban for contact lenses and finds that it is an MEQR. Both are then tested for justification and proportionality under Article 36 TFEU.

## Applying the rule
Applicability: is the measure an MEQR? Restriction or scope: is it a product requirement, a selling arrangement or a use restriction? Justification and proportionality: is there a ground under Art 36 TFEU or a mandatory requirement, and is the measure appropriate and necessary?
